soil-water-138.q: What is the main control on whether a peatland releases carbon dioxide?
soil-water-138.a: The water table: a high one submerges the peat and slows respiration, while a falling one speeds aerobic decomposition and CO2 release.

soil-water-266.q: How does a palsa begin to grow?
soil-water-266.a: Where thin snow lets frost go deeper, an ice lens draws in water and lifts the surface by frost heave, a positive feedback.

soil-water-118.q: What sets landscape ecology apart from other branches of ecology?

soil-water-261.q: Why does draining peat add to carbon dioxide emissions?
soil-water-261.a: It exposes carbon stored for thousands of years to air, where it decomposes to CO2.

soil-water-137.q: Why is a drained peatland that still has a peat layer no longer a mire?
soil-water-137.a: Because new peat no longer forms there.

soil-water-142.q: How does suffosion differ from suffusion?
soil-water-142.a: Suffosion collapses the soil structure, losing mass and volume, while suffusion removes fines from between coarse grains that stay in contact, with no change in volume.

soil-agri-013.q: Besides growing crops, name two other uses of irrigation.
soil-agri-013.a: It revegetates disturbed soils in dry areas, protects crops from frost, suppresses weeds in grain fields and prevents soil consolidation.

soil-agri-046.q: How can farmers slow the evolution of herbicide-resistant weeds?
soil-agri-046.a: By using herbicides with different modes of action.

soil-agri-049.q: In surface irrigation, what decides the depth of water applied at any point?
soil-agri-049.a: The opportunity time, how long water stands on the surface there.

soil-agri-017.q: How do self-watering containers and wicking beds supply water to plants?
soil-agri-017.a: They draw water up from a reservoir by capillary action.

soil-agri-007.q: In a crop rotation, what should precede a nitrogen-depleting crop?

soil-agri-022.q: How do catch crops reduce nitrate leaching?
soil-agri-022.a: They take up the nitrogen left over from fertilizing the previous crop, so it is not leached.

soil-agri-010.q: How does following GPS guidance lines help the soil?

soil-agri-023.q: Why does newly added phosphorus leach from soils with 'legacy phosphorus'?
soil-agri-023.a: Decades of surplus phosphorus have filled their sorption sites, so the new phosphorus cannot adsorb.

soil-agri-032.q: Why is field soil steaming only a partial disinfection?
soil-agri-032.a: Heat-resistant spore-forming bacteria survive it; true sterilization needs laboratory autoclaving.

soil-agri-036.q: Which geological raw material is used against copper deficiency, and which to conserve nitrogen?
soil-agri-036.a: Malachite against copper deficiency, and zeolite to conserve nitrogen.

soil-agri-051.q: How does surge irrigation speed the advance of water down a furrow?
soil-agri-051.a: Pulsing the flow on and off wets and dries the surface, sealing it and reducing infiltration.

soil-agri-134.q: Why are Inga trees suited to alley cropping on acid tropical soils?
soil-agri-134.a: They fix nitrogen, grow on acid tropical soils and drop a thick mulch that protects the soil and shades out weeds.

soil-agri-056.q: What compounds make brassicas useful for biofumigation?
soil-agri-056.a: Isothiocyanates released from their glucosinolates, which are toxic to soil bacteria, fungi and nematodes.

soil-agri-025.q: What unit is soil salinity most often expressed in?
soil-agri-025.a: As ECe in decisiemens per metre, formerly millimhos per centimetre.

soil-agri-106.q: Why does ploughing turn over the uppermost soil?
soil-agri-106.a: To bring fresh nutrients to the surface and bury weeds and crop remains to decay.

soil-agri-114.q: How does the soil disturbance of a harrow differ from that of a cultivator?
soil-agri-114.a: A harrow disturbs the whole surface, while a cultivator disturbs only narrow tracks between rows.

soil-agri-104.q: What might explain copper and iron deficiencies in white spruce on burned clearcuts?
soil-agri-104.a: Burning raises soil pH, and the higher pH may cause them.

soil-agri-117.q: Why may no-till delay spring planting?
soil-agri-117.a: Light-coloured residue absorbs less solar energy than bare soil, so the soil warms and dries more slowly.

soil-agri-109.q: How do a mouldboard plough's coulter and share work together?
soil-agri-109.a: The coulter cuts down into the soil and the share cuts horizontally, freeing a strip of sod that rolls over upside down.

soil-agri-107.q: Why did fields worked with an ard tend to become squarish?
soil-agri-107.a: The ard left undisturbed strips between furrows, so fields were cross-ploughed both ways.

soil-agri-115.q: How do the teeth of a toothed cultivator differ in purpose from chisel plough shanks?
soil-agri-115.a: The teeth work near the surface against weeds, while chisel shanks work deep to break hardened layers.

soil-agri-120.q: What does strip tillage combine from conventional tillage and from no-till?
soil-agri-120.a: The soil drying and warming of conventional tillage with the soil protection of no-till.

soil-agri-059.q: How does irrigation leave soils saline?
soil-agri-059.a: Salt is left behind when irrigation water evaporates or rises from shallow saline water tables.

soil-agri-140.q: How do trees in agroforestry help water enter the soil?
soil-agri-140.a: They slow runoff and evaporation, so more water infiltrates.

soil-agri-065.q: How has the view of tillage changed in conservation agriculture?
soil-agri-065.a: Once thought to raise fertility through mineralization, it is now seen to destroy organic matter and cause erosion and crusting.

soil-agri-064.q: What three things raise soil carbon sequestration?
soil-agri-064.a: More biomass inputs, smaller losses of soil organic carbon and a longer mean residence time of that carbon.

soil-agri-075.q: How does a contour trench help crops in the drier growing season?
soil-agri-075.a: It catches downhill runoff so it soaks into the soil, and crops between trenches draw on that subsoil reserve.

soil-agri-141.q: If a check dam is not mainly a sediment trap, how does it reduce erosion?
soil-agri-141.a: It flattens the channel gradient and slows the flow, which induces infiltration.

soil-agri-082.q: Where are US soil surveys published now, and how does that differ from before?
soil-agri-082.a: On the NRCS Web Soil Survey, where changes go live in moments, rather than as county books that could take years to publish.

soil-agri-089.q: How does digital soil mapping differ from traditional soil mapping?
soil-agri-089.a: Traditional mapping has field soil scientists draw boundaries by hand, while digital mapping links observations to environmental data by quantitative relationships.

soil-agri-091.q: What does pedometric mapping produce instead of polygon maps of soil types?
soil-agri-091.a: Continuous grids of measured soil properties, with maps of prediction error.

soil-env-102.q: What is the main route by which carbon dioxide leaves the atmosphere for living things?
soil-env-102.a: Photosynthesis, which moves it into land and ocean life.

soil-env-212.q: How is carbon sequestration different from carbon capture and storage?
soil-env-212.a: Carbon capture and storage separates CO2 from industrial sources and stores it underground or under the sea bed, whereas biological sequestration captures CO2 through living processes such as photosynthesis.

soil-env-111.q: Why have peatlands such as those in East Anglia and the California Delta subsided?
soil-env-111.a: Tillage and drainage exposed their organic matter to oxygen.
